premises.text: Valuable web data is trapped in HTML and most sites lack APIs that are hard to build
premises.evidence_span: The majority of sites do not have an API, and creating one is complex

premises.text: Non-developers can turn any website into a table or API in minutes without writing code
premises.evidence_span: turn any website. into a table of data or an API in a matter of minutes without writing code

premises.text: Example-based extraction generalizes rows and columns into a live cloud API
premises.evidence_span: it generalizes from these examples to learn where all the rows are on the page

premises.text: Multiple site APIs combine into one call for scaled live data into applications
premises.evidence_span: Combining the API that I just created with other APIs is very easy. I simply choose the ones I want, and I now have jobs data from hundreds of company websites streaming straight into my application over a single API call

premises.text: Data Factory Chrome extension gives anyone the library of prebuilt APIs or request ones
premises.evidence_span: The data factory is a chrome extension that will allow anybody to get access to our library of APIs or requests that won't be built

value.text: Web data becomes easily accessible so anyone can use it
value.evidence_span: data on the web would be easily accessible to everyone

secondary_value.text: Better decisions, government accountability, and personal safety from released data
secondary_value.evidence_span: help you make better informed decisions at work, ensure you had the information to hold your government accountable, and even make sure you got home safely after a good night out

causal_links.evidence_span: this data is not available to everyone
instantly, the data is extracted from the site

notes: Singleton D3 retained: Data Factory is launched as a separately revisable access product with its own path to value (§4.1(5) split warrant). 'Every website has an API' future belief coded as vision/framing not a premise (§4.1(4)). User/API/page counts and free tier treated as traction/pricing promo. Red Cross and HP stories illustrate P2/P3, not new premises.
